Harley-Davidson Sends Three Fresh ST Baggers Our Way, Road King and More Are Back for 2027
6 photos
Photo: Harley-Davidson
For years now, American bike maker Harley-Davidson has gotten us used to releasing the bikes for the new model year in January. While this habit still stands, the Milwaukee crew went off program this week and announced the arrival of three new motorcycles for 2027, but also a few details on what we are to expect in the coming months.
At the core of Harley-Davidson's announcement remain the three new Grand American Touring models being offered. Not new in the sense that they are just now entering the lineup, but new in that, despite being based on existing bikes, are still fresh enough to get hearts pumping.
The trio comprises ST versions of the Road Glide , Street Glide, and the returning Road King. They are very closely related, as they share many of their component parts, including the Showa suspension system and the Brembo braking hardware.
Also common is the powertrain, which would be the Milwaukee-Eight 117 High Output engine, modified to deliver 12 percent more horsepower than the standard Milwaukee-Eight 117 engine. That would be a total of 115 hp for the two Glides, and slightly more, 117 hp, for the Road King.
Photo: Harley-Davidson The Road is perhaps the most exciting of the bunch, as it makes a comeback at the end of a relatively brief hiatus. And it comes back with visual changes as well, including a redesigned headlamp nacelle, reshaped bodywork, and a low-profile console.
All three motorcycles in their 2027 model year guise are already listed as available on the bike maker's U.S. configurator, but only one of them, the Road King, also shows a price sticker – that would be $24,999 for this two-wheeler. We'll keep an eye out for when pricing for the two Glides becomes public.
The three new STs are part of the company's plan to expand its offering for the new model year, but they are not the only changes that were announced. As you'll see below, there is talk of new colors, a new special collection, and hints of a bunch of insane CVO models.
When it comes to the colors it offers for its bikes, Harley announced that, at the request of customers, Vivid Black now becomes the base paint color for most of the lineup, kicking the current Dark Billiard Gray from this role.
Photo: Harley-Davidson Also new is something called the Lunar Divide, a paint scheme that brings together Vivid Black and Black Denim for a two-tone approach, and offsets that with the help of Medium Red pinstripes. If you like the idea, don't get your hopes up, as this design will only be offered for the Low Rider S and Low Rider ST models.
The new Lunar Divide paint scheme from Harley-Davidson Factory Custom Paint & Graphics, available only for the Low Rider® S and Low Rider® ST motorcycles, is composed of a dynamic split Vivid Black/Black Denim two-tone with a Medium Red pinstripe parting line executed in a reverse scallop design.'
I mentioned something about a special collection earlier in the story. It's called Iron & Ink, and it is a way of painting the bodies of some Harley bikes while at the same time paying tribute to the tattoo culture and its creations.
Iron & Ink uses deep red Oxblood Metallic as a base color, and matches that with a dedicated windscreen and hand-crafted detailing of new and iconic elements, including the Bar & Shield logo and the V-twin engine silhouette. Harley promises references to the bison of the Black Hills and the water tower at Harley's Juneau Avenue HQ, among others.
Photo: Harley-Davidson The special paint job will only be available on the Street Glide and Road Glide bikes in black trim, and only 2,000 of them will be made for each of the models. The offering is part of the Enthusiast Collection and will set people back $27,999 for the Street and $28,999 for the Road.
Last but not least, Harley mentioned a thing or two about the CVO lineup for the 2027 model year, without going too deep into the details. We are to expect a collection of five limited-production performance machines: the CVO Road Glide, CVO Street Glide ST , CVO Road Glide ST, CVO Street Glide Limited, and CVO Street Glide 3 Limited.
Harley let loose the fact that the bikes are packed with new Screamin’ Eagle/Ohlins front and rear suspension parts and Brembo Hypure braking components. There will be six exclusive new design and paint schemes on the table, but we're not being told anything about them yet.
The Harley cruiser range gets an upgrade as well, with an eight-model strong family now on the table. It is throwing into the fight the Super Glide that was born earlier this year as a limited-production bike, but is now turning into a global model, the Deadwood, the Low Rider S and ST, and, of course, the almighty Breakout, Heritage Classic, Fat Boy, and Street Bob.
